newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan investment banking on growth path.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan investment banking on growth path.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc, as expected, reported a sharp decline in trading revenue for the second quarter but analysts noted the shortfall was partly offset by gains in investment banking revenue, which is a good sign for the future, analysts said.

"Investment banking is a blockbuster," said analyst George Salem of Gerard Klauer Mattison. "They're continuing to prove that they are on the verge of bulge bracket status up there with the best." Salem said overall the earnings were a "pleassant surprise" and the investment banking gains were significant because the area is an important part of the company's future.
Trading revenue fell to $477 million from $697 million both in the first quarter of 1997 and the first quarter of 1977. The weak trading results had been expected by analysts.
Investment banking revenue rose to $294 million from $210 million in the year-ago quarter and $226 million in the first quarter of 1997.

Raphael Soifer, analyst at Brown Brothers Harriman, noted that in the second quarter J.P. Morgan ranked 11th worldwide in lead-managed equity underwritings and was fifth in combined U.S. debt and equity underwriting.

"We are encourged by the continuing growth in client-related revenues, which augers well for the long term future although the steady pace of investment spending is holding near-term profits," Soifer said in a research note. "The balance of J.P. Morgan's business mix is continuing to swing toward client-focused businesses, which, we believe, will benefit the shares' valuation going forward."
Overall, J.P. Morgan said second-quarter net income was $374 million, or $1.85 per share, compared to $440 million or $2.14 per share a year ago.
Soifer noted that J.P. Morgan had a better-than-expected performance in its equity investments, with $124 million in revenue versus $126 million a year ago.
J.P. Morgan said the revenues included net gains of $118 million mostly related to the sale of equity investments in the communications and insurance industries.
